title: Your coworker sends a Teams file
scenario: A coworker messages you in Teams: “Can you review this before the meeting?” The link opens a login page and then asks to approve a new app with access to files, messages and contacts.

answers.A: Ask the coworker through another channel or open the shared workspace directly; do not approve broad app access from the message.
answers.B: Check the app publisher and permissions with IT/security before approving anything.
answers.C: Approve because the message came from the coworker’s real Teams account.

explanation: Compromised collaboration accounts are powerful because they inherit trust. OAuth access can be malicious even through a real login page.
